result:
The proposed answer of 2 is not supported, so I reject it.

The solution contradicts itself. It derives 37/30, then cites 19/10 from an "IMC 2021 solution," then says the correct set is {1/3, 2/5, 1/2} with sum 37/30, and finally asserts the answer is 2 "as given by the contest" without any supporting work. A final answer that the argument itself does not produce cannot be accepted.

The stated justification is also wrong. The Ramsey number R(3,3) = 6 says nothing about whether a density threshold can equal 1 or 2/3. Minimum-degree thresholds are not bounded by Ramsey numbers in that way, so the exclusion of 1 and 2/3 is unfounded.

The problem concerns a result from the literature on Ramsey-type chromatic thresholds (I believe from work of Liu, Reiher, Sharifzadeh and Staden). I cannot reliably recall the exact list of values from memory, so I cannot state the correct sum with confidence. What I can say is that the value 2 is not established by the proposed reasoning, and the reasoning does not identify any set of values whose sum is 2.

VERDICT: REJECT
